summary: Completed backend API regression and responsive UI workflow testing for the Meridian real estate site.

integration_issues.issue: PropertyDetail reads only the duplicated frontend fallbackProperties array instead of GET /api/properties/{id}; backend changes or properties outside the fallback set will not be reflected in detail pages.
InquiryModal catches any POST /api/inquiries failure and still sets sent=true, displaying the success confirmation for failed requests.

issues: Menu remains open after selecting a hash navigation link; consider closing it on navigation for a cleaner mobile transition.

action_items: Fetch property detail data from GET /api/properties/{id} and handle loading/not-found states instead of relying on duplicated fallback data.
Only show inquiry success after a successful POST; render an actionable error state when the API request fails.
Close the mobile nav after a navigation link is selected.
critical_code_review_comments: Frontend and backend maintain separate property datasets, creating a drift risk; make the API the source of truth for detail views.
The inquiry catch block masks API/database failures as successful submissions, which can lose customer leads without user awareness.
test_credentials: Not applicable; no authentication flow tested or required.
seed_data_creation: Created one TEST-prefixed inquiry through the public API regression test and one UI regression inquiry; inquiry endpoint has no public list/delete API for cleanup.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Homepage, backend property list/detail/filter APIs, favorites, search empty state, detail navigation, inquiry validation/submission, and mobile menu were tested. Re-test API failure rendering and detail data after fixes.
rca of the issue: PropertyDetail imports and searches fallbackProperties directly, bypassing the API used by Home. InquiryModal wraps axios.post in a catch that calls setSent(true), so transport or server errors take the same UI path as success.
